_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one. status: active = connector-only, a reprint would clobber it; upstreamed = also fixed in the press, a reprint from a fixed press regenerates it, but the back-port must still be present today.

handfixes.summary: `golang.org/x/text` is pinned at v0.41.0, above the v0.39.0 fix for GO-2026-5970
handfixes.why: The press emits `golang.org/x/text v0.14.0` as an indirect dependency of modernc.org/sqlite. Every version below v0.39.0 carries GO-2026-5970 (CVE-2026-56852): a norm.Iter infinite loop on input containing invalid UTF-8 bytes. Because a new connector's go.mod counts as introducing every version in it, the repo security gate scores that advisory P1 and blocks the merge. A reprint from a press that still emits v0.14.0 reintroduces the P1.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Raise the floor on golang.org/x/text in the press module template so generated go.mod files ship above the GO-2026-5970 fix by construction (filed as a retro item against the generator).

handfixes.summary: the MCP tenant gate falls through to the tool handler when no platform source is registered, instead of default-denying every non-mirror tool
handfixes.why: cli.VerifyMCPInvocation returns (nil, nil) when registeredPlatformSource is nil, which means 'there is nothing to gate' - and no connector in this repo registers a platform source (registerPlatformSource has zero callers outside internal/cli/platform_client.go). The 4.30.1/4.30.2 gate read that nil session as a failure and answered 'MCP tenant gate is not configured' for every tool that is not a Cobra mirror. Cobra mirrors carry pp:tenant-gate = "child-cli" and pass through, so the damage was invisible in a tool count: 5 tools on this connector were dead while the server still listed them. Those 5 are the entire offline-mirror surface (context, search, sql) plus the code-orchestration surface (avanan_search, avanan_get) - exactly the capabilities this connector's own description says a plain read-only MCP does not ship. Measured with check_mcp_gate.py before the fix: all 5 were reported DEFAULT-DENIED; after, none are. Fixed upstream in cli-printing-press 4.30.3 (issue #4157, PR #4171); this is the surgical back-port, byte-identical to what 4.30.3 emits and to the same back-port already merged on cork. TestMCPUngatedInvocationUsesRealVerifier is the regression test that ships with the 4.30.3 template: it drives the wrapper with the REAL verifier (not the fake the other two tests install) and fails if the handler is blocked. Reverting either the fall-through or the test fails check_handfixes.py.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Already fixed in the press at 4.30.3 (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#4171). A reprint on 4.30.3 or later regenerates both the fall-through and the conformance test, so this entry exists to keep the back-port from being dropped by a reprint on an older engine or by a regen-merge that resurrects the 4.30.2 body.

asserts.not_contains: NewToolResultError("MCP tenant gate is not configured")

handfixes.summary: x-av-date is sent as microsecond precision with no zone suffix, because the server parses the value and returns HTTP 500 on a trailing Z
handfixes.why: avanansig.DateFormat originally used "2006-01-02T15:04:05.000Z" on the reasoning that the vendor's samples are inconsistent and any format works so long as the header and the signed preimage are byte-identical. That reasoning is wrong: the server parses x-av-date rather than echoing it, and a trailing Z makes the parse fail. The API then answers HTTP 500 for every request, including one carrying a deliberately fabricated app id, so the failure presents as a vendor outage or an unprovisioned credential rather than a client bug. Verified live against smart-api-production-1-us on 2026-08-20: microsecond precision with no zone suffix returns a JWT, millisecond precision with Z returns 500, and x-av-token is irrelevant in both cases. This matches Avanan's own MSP sample client, which sends datetime.datetime.utcnow().isoformat(). The "2021-04-10T00:00:00.000Z" literal in the API Reference Guide is the input to the guide's worked signature example, not an accepted x-av-date value.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press has no way to express "this header is parsed by the server, so the layout is load-bearing". If a date-format annotation is ever added, encode it on the security scheme rather than leaving it to a hand-fix.

handfixes.summary: the generated commands no longer refuse to run without --x-av-req-id or --scopes; both are supplied by the transport or decided by the API
handfixes.why: The press promoted two parameters to required CLI flags on 32 commands. x-av-req-id is a per-request transport header that AvananTransport already generates and sets (avanan_transport.go), so demanding it from the caller asks for a value the client is about to overwrite. --scopes is worse: it was required on the `scopes` command itself, whose entire job is to discover which scopes a credential reaches, so the only way to list your scopes was to already know one. The API is the correct enforcement point and answers a multi-scope client with HTTP 400 naming the requirement, which the connector already surfaces. 47 enforcement blocks were removed across 32 files; the flags themselves remain available for callers who want to pin a scope or correlate a request id.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press should not promote a security-scheme or transport-generated header to a required command flag, and should not mark a discovery endpoint's own filter parameter required.

handfixes.summary: the entity mirror sends requestData.entityFilter with a saas value and the window inside it, one pass per platform
handfixes.why: Entities and Events shared one request builder that sent a flat {startDate, scopes, pageSize} requestData. That is correct for /v1.0/event/query and wrong for /v1.0/search/query, which requires requestData.entityFilter and reads the window from inside it. The endpoint answered HTTP 422 with 'entityFilter Field required' and the entity mirror stored zero rows on every run while the command still reported success. The endpoint also accepts exactly one saas per query, so a full entity mirror is one pass per platform rather than a single call; EntitySaaS carries the nine platform identifiers and a per-platform failure no longer empties the whole mirror.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press generated the correct nested entityFilter for the query-saas-entity command from the spec but the hand-written mirror did not reuse it. If the mirror is ever regenerated, take the body shape from the generated command rather than from the event query.

handfixes.summary: mirror resolves an empty --scope to the credential's real scope list instead of issuing one unscoped request
handfixes.why: Options.Scopes documents empty as 'every scope the credential can reach', but Exceptions turned an empty list into a single request carrying no scope param. A multi-scope app client rejects that on all nine exception sub-systems and the sectool paths with HTTP 400 'Must provide a single scope in as scope in query string due to multi scope app client', so the documented behaviour and the implemented behaviour disagreed and the exception mirror stored nothing for a multi-tenant MSP. DiscoverScopes reads GET /v1.0/scopes and the mirror command resolves the list before building Options, so the per-scope fan-out Exceptions already implements is actually reached. Discovery failure warns and continues rather than aborting, because a single-scope credential does not need it.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: None. This is a behavioural contract between two hand-written pieces, not a spec gap.
